Abstract
Background/Aims: To evaluate the prevalence of ptosis, strabismus and the combination of both after glaucoma surgery and determine which kind of surgery is most likely to be linked to these complications.
Methods: A total of 705 clinical records of patients who underwent glaucoma surgery at the University Eye Clinic of IRCCS Ospedale Policlinico San Martino, Genoa, from January 1, 2010, to December 31, 2020, were retrospectively evaluated. Results: Out of all patients 26 developed ptosis alone (3.7%), two developed bilateral ptosis, with a mean of 2.2 ± 1.08 procedures per patient. Twelve patients developed strabismus alone (1,7%), four underwent unilateral surgery and eight bilateral surgery, with an average of 3.3 ± 1.78 procedures per patient. Ocular movement abnormalities and ptosis after glaucoma surgery: A retrospective decade long analysis
Abstract
Background/Aims: To evaluate the prevalence of ptosis, strabismus and the combination of both after glaucoma surgery and determine which kind of surgery is most likely to be linked to these complications.
Methods: A total of 705 clinical records of patients who underwent glaucoma surgery at the University Eye Clinic of IRCCS Ospedale Policlinico San Martino, Genoa, from January 1, 2010, to December 31, 2020, were retrospectively evaluated. Surgery procedures were divided in three groups: “Ab interno”, “Ab externo” and “Muscle isolation”.
Results: Out of all patients 26 developed ptosis alone (3.7%), two developed bilateral ptosis, with a mean of 2.2 ± 1.08 procedures per patient. Highest incidence of ptosis was noticed in patients who underwent muscle isolation surgery (5.7%). Twelve patients developed strabismus alone (1,7%), four underwent unilateral surgery and eight bilateral surgery, with an average of 3.3 ± 1.78 procedures per patient.
